The strongest evidence-backed change is to restore the reliability-correction coefficient from `0.02` to `0.04`. In the supplied results, this improved combined score from `0.9287` to `0.9301`, reduced false-clear from `0.0471` to `0.0377`, and improved all ranking metrics. False-block increased to `0.0955`, so this is not a universal diagnostic improvement, but it respects the hard requirement not to sacrifice false-clear.

The interaction only modifies risk when approach and expansion corroborate one another. Consistency and observation quality determine whether that shared motion evidence receives a small boost or discount. This preserves the simple exposure baseline, clips negative motion observations, remains deterministic and finite for normalized inputs, and keeps the known 96-node complexity profile.
